mailflow-export-astrbot.name: AstrBot Exporter
mailflow-export-astrbot.description: Exports a configured MailFlow instance as an AstrBot plugin
mailflow-export-astrbot.readme:
# AstrBot exporter

Exporter ID: `astrbot`. Creates a framework host from the current MailFlow
configuration without starting a mail runtime during export.

```bash
uv run mailflow export --framework astrbot --output dist/astrbot_plugin_mailflow -c configs/local.toml
```

Install the generated folder through your AstrBot plugin workflow and enable it. Configure MailFlow administrators through the matching enabled notifier binding described in the generated README; framework administrator flags are not imported automatically.
The generated README describes its file layout and command prefix. Its host
starts/stops the MailFlow service with the framework and forwards sender/chat identity to the shared layer.
Administration is resolved from a unique enabled notifier matching the platform
and instance, with the sender in options.admins; unmatched providers remain read-only.

Supported framework file events can upload managed files, and supported adapters
can send selected files back. Availability depends on the actual platform adapter;
exporting/importing Python successfully does not prove file delivery. Mutations
and sending keep their permission and confirmation rules.

The exported configuration is a snapshot, not a live link. Environment-backed
secrets remain references; literal credentials may still be present. Review the
output, supply needed environment variables in the bot host and regenerate after
configuration changes. Configured notifiers deliver notifications: the export
adapter does not imply an extra automatic broadcast to every framework chat.

mailflow-llm-anthropic.description: Chat-completions transport for Anthropic Claude (Messages API)
mailflow-llm-anthropic.readme:
# Anthropic Messages backend

Component IDs: `anthropic-messages` and compatible alias `anthropic`. Translates
the shared chat/tool format into Messages requests and returns structured tool calls.

```toml
[[llms]]
llm_id = "primary"
provider = "anthropic"
model = "your-model-id"
api_key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

[llms.options]
max_tokens = 2048
```

The default endpoint is `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`. A top-level
`base_url` may name a proxy root, `/v1` prefix or complete `/messages` endpoint;
legacy `options.base_url` is a complete endpoint override. `options.max_tokens`
defaults to 1024. Optional `thinking_budget` requests a budget supported by the
selected model and raises the output cap as needed.

Standard timeout, retry, headers, query and extra-body configuration applies.
The backend accepts temperature, per-call options and tools; the selected model
must support the requested features. Choose a currently available model ID and
check credentials/endpoint on failure. Do not put real keys in configuration
examples or logs. Model ordering and fallback use the shared MailFlow settings.

# Google Generative AI backend

Component ID: `google-generative-ai`. Uses Gemini `generateContent`, translating
system messages and structured tool calls from the shared MailFlow contract.

```toml
[[llms]]
llm_id = "primary"
provider = "google-generative-ai"
model = "your-model-id"
api_key_env = "GEMINI_API_KEY"
```

The default root is `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`; `base_url`
overrides it for a compatible proxy. Requests use
`/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` and the `x-goog-api-key` header.
`options.max_tokens`, `temperature` and `thinking_budget` set optional generation
defaults. Standard headers/query, `extra_body`, timeout and retry settings apply.

Use a model available to your account. Tool and generation capabilities depend
on that model; connection/parameter failures remain visible and can fall back
through the configured model chain. This plugin is an API transport, not a
browser-login integration.

mailflow-llm-google-vertex.readme:
# Google Vertex AI backend

Component ID: `google-vertex`. Sends shared chat/tool requests to Vertex
`generateContent`. A project and a valid access credential are required.

```toml
[[llms]]
llm_id = "primary"
provider = "google-vertex"
model = "your-model-id"
api_key_env = "VERTEX_ACCESS_TOKEN"

[llms.options]
project = "your-project-id"
location = "us-central1"
```

`options.project` is required; location defaults to `us-central1`. `base_url`
defaults to `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com`. Authentication uses a short-lived
OAuth access token in `api_key`/`api_key_env`, or
`options.service_account_file` with `google-auth` installed in the host.
An ordinary API key is not an OAuth token. Keep service-account files private.

Optional `max_tokens`, `temperature` and `thinking_budget` generation defaults,
shared headers/query/extra body, timeout and retry are supported. Select a model
and location available to your project; the transport does not grant project
access. Failed credentials or unsupported capabilities are reported normally.

mailflow-llm-openai-compatible.readme:
# OpenAI-compatible model backends

Provides Chat Completions and Responses transports, including configured proxy
and Azure endpoints. Component IDs: `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`,
`openai-codex-responses`, `azure-openai-responses`; `openai-compatible` is the
compatible Chat Completions alias.

```toml
[[llms]]
llm_id = "primary"
provider = "openai-compatible"
base_url = "https://your-provider.example/v1"
model = "your-model-id"
api_key_env = "MAILFLOW_MODEL_KEY"
timeout_seconds = 60
max_retries = 2
```

Choose the transport supported by your endpoint. `openai-codex-responses` selects
a Responses request format, not account login or a subscription credential flow.
Azure uses the deployment name as `model` and the resource address as `base_url`.
Its `options.api_version` defaults to the transport's `preview` value; set a value
accepted by your endpoint.

| Configuration | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `api_key` / `api_key_env` | Literal/environment credential; environment references are preferred |
| `headers`, `query`, `extra_body` | Additional configured headers, URL parameters and JSON body fields |
| `timeout_seconds`, `max_retries` | Request timeout and retry policy |
| `options.path` | Override the transport-specific `chat/completions` or `responses` path |
| `options.max_tokens`, `options.temperature`, `options.stream` | Optional request defaults where supported by the chosen transport/model |

The shared chat contract accepts temperature, per-call options and tools, and
returns text plus structured tool calls. The actual model/endpoint must support
the requested capability. Use model IDs available to your account, not a fixed
example alias. Valid explicit processor llm/fallback_llms bindings take priority. Otherwise the marked default (or first entry) is primary, and unspecified fallbacks use the remaining list. Test a
connection before requesting analysis; authentication or unsupported parameters
are reported as failures, not empty successful completions.

mailflow-mail-fake.readme:
# Fake mail source

Provides deterministic messages for local development and demonstrations without
connecting to a mailbox. Component ID: `fake`.

```toml
[[accounts]]
account_id = "demo"
provider = "fake"
email = "demo@local.test"

[accounts.options]
base_time = "2026-01-01T08:00:00+00:00"
mails = [{ message_id = "welcome", subject = "Welcome", sender = "team@example.com", body = "Your workspace is ready." }]
```

`mails` accepts `message_id`, `subject`, `sender`, `sender_name`, `body`,
`body_html` and an optional `urgency` hint. Keep message IDs stable to exercise
retry deduplication. Timestamps use `base_time` plus the message index in minutes.
`fail = true` and `delay` (seconds) simulate source failures and slow handoff.
This is a development source, not a way to send real email.

mailflow-mail-imap.readme:
# IMAP mail source

Receives IMAP mail and sends through SMTP. Component ID: `imap`. Presets are
`qq`, `163`, `gmail` and `outlook`; explicit hosts override the preset.

```toml
[[accounts]]
account_id = "personal"
provider = "imap"
email = "you@example.com"
state_sync = false

[accounts.options]
imap_host = "imap.example.com"
smtp_host = "smtp.example.com"
password = "${MAIL_PASSWORD}"
initial_sync = "new"
catch_up_missed = false
```

| Option | Default / purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `preset` | Optional server preset; otherwise set `imap_host` and the needed send host |
| `username` / `password` | Account email / required mailbox credential |
| `imap_port`, `imap_ssl`, `imap_folder` | `993`, `true`, `INBOX` |
| `smtp_port`, `smtp_ssl` | `465`; implicit TLS on 465, STARTTLS otherwise unless overridden |
| `initial_sync`, `initial_days` | `new`; `recent` imports 30 days by default, `all` explicitly imports history |
| `catch_up_missed`, `catch_up_summary` | `false` / `true`; optional catch-up from a valid saved cursor, normally with a summary |
| `include_past_actions` | `false`; opt in to past tasks from imported mail |
| `interval_seconds`, `limit` | `300` / `20`; polling interval and batch size, not implicit startup history |
| `archive_folder`, `trash_folder`, `sent_folder` | Optional overrides for detected source folders |

The default first connection receives only new mail. History browsing is separate;
restarts do not resume abandoned analysis. A valid account/folder-scoped UID and
UIDVALIDITY cursor is required for missed-mail catch-up; invalid progress asks for
an explicit resync range. Accepted messages advance progress only after handoff.

Account IDs isolate mail identity. MIME attachment bytes survive extraction, and
attachments can be fetched on demand independently of OCR. Receiving and sending
must be checked separately. Configured credentials must be accepted by the mail
service; presets do not implement native OAuth.

Optional account `state_sync` enables supported read/star/archive synchronization.
Source trash/restore requires confirmation and a reliable move capability; unknown
results are checked before retry. Local permanent deletion never expunges source
mail. See the [operation guide](https://github.com/Kingcxp/mailflow/blob/dev/docs/configuration/overview.md).

# Console notifications

The `console` channel delivers mail notifications, task reminders and summaries to the TUI **Console** tab. No external account, gateway or login is required.

```toml
[[notifiers]]
notifier_id = "console"
provider = "console"
minimum_urgency = "important"
```

The Console tab accepts existing MailFlow commands. Use `@MailFlow` or quote a message to request an intelligent operation. Changes and sending still require chat confirmation. Ordinary text does not invoke a model.

Messages remain in memory for the current service run. Detach and reconnect keep them; stopping the service clears them. Notification switches, quiet hours and delivery receipts still apply.

Outside the TUI, console logging remains available when enabled. Images fall back to text.

mailflow-notify-onebot.readme:
# OneBot / QQ notifier and chat connection

Component ID: `onebot`. Supports mail delivery and shared text-based
reminders/commands; images and managed files are available through the channel's
rich-message capabilities and platform limits.

```toml
[[notifiers]]
notifier_id = "onebot-main"
provider = "onebot"
minimum_urgency = "important"

[notifiers.options]
http_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3000"
access_token = "${ONEBOT_ACCESS_TOKEN}"
targets = ["user:123456"]
admins = ["123456"]
```

Use an existing OneBot v11 HTTP service or the matching managed gateway. Installation, process startup, QQ login and delivery readiness are separate steps; follow detected prerequisites and scan/login when requested.

`http_url` is required. `access_token` must match the gateway. Targets use `user:<id>` or `group:<id>`; administrators use stable platform user IDs. HTTP 200 with a failing OneBot retcode is a failure.

Administrator identity controls mutations, sending, configuration and plugin
management. Ordinary allowed read commands do not require making everyone an
administrator. Natural-language management uses the shared assistant and requires
a configured model; changes and outbound mail retain confirmation checks.

Fixed targets and chat subscriptions are distinct. Unsubscribing reports whether
a separately configured fixed target still receives pushes. Global, channel and
chat switches, urgency and quiet hours determine actual delivery. Optional
`notification_images`, `summary_cards` and `send_interval_seconds` use the shared
notification settings; text is the fallback on unsupported output.

Configuration, HTTP and platform errors fail delivery visibly. Per-target
receipts prevent retries from repeating successful destinations. Run a delivery
test after login; process existence alone does not prove the connection works.

mailflow-storage-sqlite.readme:
# SQLite storage

Component ID: `sqlite`. Stores mail, analysis, tasks, drafts, preferences and
recoverable trash in one local database, with compatible incremental migrations.

```toml
[storage]
provider = "sqlite"
path = "data/mailflow.db"
```

Parent directories are created as needed. `:memory:` is temporary and disappears
when closed. Retention is controlled by `[general]`, not fixed by this plugin;
mail defaults to indefinite retention and trash to seven days. Trash restore
preserves stored mail state and ingestion origin. Receipt-date filtering uses
the source mail timestamp. Reanalysis retains manual priority and local state.

Mail records keep text/HTML, attachment metadata and OCR text. Managed uploads
and fetched attachment caches are stored separately from those records and are
included by the service backup workflow when available. Uncached attachments
still need source access.

Use MailFlow backup/restore for a consistent portable archive and recovery
preview. If manually copying a database, stop its writer first; copying only
the main file while WAL is active is not a consistent backup.

# OpenWechat notifications

Add an OpenWechat channel from Notifications and use the setup guide to install the gateway and scan its login QR code. Ordinary notification settings do not require a new login.

For an existing gateway, configure `gateway_url`. Contacts use `contact:<stable-id>` and rooms use `room:<stable-id>`. Configure administrator platform IDs rather than display names.

Notification, image and command support depends on the gateway. Failed delivery is recorded for retry; management operations use the shared permission and confirmation rules.

mailflow-notify-wechatpadpro.readme:
# WeChatPadPro notifications

Add this channel in Notifications and use the guide to install, start and log in, or connect an existing gateway.

`base_url` is the gateway endpoint. External gateways accept `auth_key` or can mint it using `admin_key`. MailFlow-managed credentials remain in the instance directory instead of the editable notifier configuration.

Use `user:<wxid>` or `group:<chatroom_id>` targets and platform account IDs for administrators. An HTTP response alone does not prove login or delivery readiness. Missing credentials, network errors and platform rejection are recorded for retry.
